increment_paragraph: **NAME-KEYED-HOLDER-SHADOWING** (USER DECISION 2026-11-25, "lanich four of queued cards"; gateway rule 86; `QCore.NameKeyedHolderShadowing`; [report](../../reports/name-keyed-holder-shadowing/README.md)). Discharges `NAME-KEYED-HOLDER-SHADOWING` (registered by FRAME-HOLDER-SHADOWED-NAME). Rule 12t's formal-keyed readings (a retained formal or its interior as a caller's object, a path holder below a formal, a removal keyed on either) decided from the token census `CallerFormals::contains`. Probed at each with inner-block, for-init, pointer, array, typedef'd-array and `__auto_type` shadows, every shape refused at base at the classifier's shadow guard (S, M, H). Declarations the guard does not recognize (`__attribute__`, `_Alignas`, `__typeof__`, parenthesized, enumeration constants) refused incidentally (U1-U16). But a shadow whose declaration a `switch` or `goto` jumps over puts the guard on no path: the shadow was read as the formal, the route reached `Safe`, and only the internal certificate check rejected the unit (J1-J9). Each reading now also requires the name to be one declaration, the `ParmVarDecl` every `DeclRefExpr` of the name designates (`legacy_formal_declaration.rs`). A name that fails is a plain name (`retention-undecided`), its path no path holder, and its removal unmatched. Lean: `no_verdict_becomes_safe` by a record-cover simulation over `QCore.RetentionPath`; J2 and J6 are `Safe` under rule 12t's reading and refused now. `tests/name_keyed_holder_shadowing.rs` (5 passed, 1 failed at base; 6 passed at tip). Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6, each side on its own tree and binary: base 43410b230 and tip 182767251 both 1,187/2/3,607/8 with no changed row, as predicted. Scoped gate at 182767251: every step 0 except the Rust suite (10,113 passed, 6 failed, exactly the six known K5-LOCAL-ORIGIN-ALIASES base failures); 509 Lean audits; 807 Python tests. Pinned routes are not runnable on the host; no move predicted. Follow-up `JUMPED-SHADOW-FORMAL-READINGS` (the guard's two gaps at the other formal-keyed consumers, unassessed).

ledger.why: Discharged by NAME-KEYED-HOLDER-SHADOWING (rule 86). Probed at every formal-keyed reading of rule 12t (retained formal, interior, path holder, removal) with inner-block, for-init, pointer, array, typedef'd-array and __auto_type shadows: each refuses at base at the classifier's shadow guard, and declarations the guard does not recognize (__attribute__, _Alignas, __typeof__, a parenthesized declarator, an enumeration constant) refuse by incidental routes. A shadow whose declaration a switch or goto jumps over puts the guard's refusal on no path: the shadow was read as the formal and the verdict was Safe on its paths, stopped only by the internal certificate check (probes J1-J9, failing at base). Each formal-keyed reading now also requires the name to be one declaration, the ParmVarDecl every DeclRefExpr of the name designates (legacy_formal_declaration.rs every_reference_is_the_formal), so J1-J9 refuse at the reading (retention-undecided) and the controls stay Safe; pinned in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/name_keyed_holder_shadowing.rs (5 passed, 1 failed at base; 6 passed at tip). The path holder was also protected by its own census (the shadow's declarator is a bare mention of the root). QCore.NameKeyedHolderShadowing: no_verdict_becomes_safe by a record-cover simulation over QCore.RetentionPath, with the J2 and J6 witnesses.

ledger.title: Formal-keyed readings outside rule 12t rest on the shadow guard, which a jumped-over declaration bypasses
ledger.text: Found by NAME-KEYED-HOLDER-SHADOWING. The classifier's guard (legacy_classify.rs, `local declaration may shadow a formal resource identity`) refuses a declaration statement that names a formal, but (a) a declaration control jumps over (before a switch's first label, past a goto target) puts that refusal on no path, and (b) a declaration opening with __attribute__, _Alignas or __typeof__, or a parenthesized declarator, is not recognized as one and is refused only incidentally (an uncontracted call, an indirect access). Rule 86 closed rule 12t's readings. Every other consumer of CallerFormals (container publication, member custody attribution, slot moves, descriptor cells' formal closure, legacy_classify) and the W4 entry custody of formals still decide from the formal's spelling. For rule 12t the jumped shapes reached Safe on their paths and only the internal certificate check rejected the unit (fail-closed, an error, not a verdict); the other consumers are not probed. Direction not assessed. DISCHARGE: probe a jumped-over and an unrecognized shadow at each other formal-keyed consumer; where one reaches Safe, require the declaration reading (rule 86's every_reference_is_the_formal) or make the guard read Clang's declarations, and pin the shape.
